deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a French copy of Riemann's 1859 Berlin Monatsberichte paper 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse' (previous page: title, Euler product, and Π(s-1)ζ(s)=∫_0^∞ x^{s-1}/(e^x-1)dx with Π(s-1)=Γ(s)). This page carries out the analytic continuation of ζ by a loop integral and starts the derivation of the functional equation.

(1) Loop integral. Consider J(s)=∫ (-x)^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx taken from +∞ to +∞, positively (counterclockwise) around a region containing x=0 but no other singularity of the integrand (the poles x=2πin, n≠0, stay outside). The branch is (-x)^{s-1}=exp((s-1)log(-x)), with log(-x) real for negative x, i.e. arg(-x) in (-π,π), cut along the positive real x-axis.
[My filling:] Come in from +∞ to 0 just above the axis, where arg x=0+, arg(-x)=-π, so (-x)^{s-1}=x^{s-1}e^{-iπ(s-1)}. Circle the origin counterclockwise; the small circle contributes nothing when Re s>1. Go out to +∞ just below the axis, where arg(-x)=+π, so (-x)^{s-1}=x^{s-1}e^{iπ(s-1)}. Adding the two sides gives
J=(e^{iπ(s-1)}-e^{-iπ(s-1)})·I=(e^{-iπs}-e^{iπs})·I, with I=∫_0^∞ x^{s-1}/(e^x-1)dx. This is exactly the page's formula.

(2) Since e^{-iπs}-e^{iπs}=-2i sin πs and I=Π(s-1)ζ(s), multiplying by i gives
2 sin(πs) Π(s-1) ζ(s) = i∫_∞^∞ (-x)^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx,
i.e. ζ(s)=Γ(1-s)/(2πi)·∫_C (-x)^{s-1}/(e^x-1)dx.

(3) Consequences claimed. The loop integral converges for all s and is entire, so this gives ζ for every complex s and shows it is single-valued.
- Finiteness: 1/(sin πs Γ(s))=Γ(1-s)/π has poles only at s=1,2,3,…
- At s=2,3,… the integrand is single-valued and holomorphic at 0, so the integral vanishes and ζ stays finite.
- At s=1 the integrand has residue 1 at 0, so ζ has a pole there.
- At s=-m (m≥1) a residue computation [mine] gives ζ(-m)=(-1)^m B_{m+1}/(m+1). This vanishes for even m only, i.e. s=-2,-4,…

(4) For Re s<0, one may instead take the integral negatively around the complement of the region, which contains the poles 2πin, n≠0. This is allowed because the contribution of the arcs at large |x| tends to 0 when Re s<0. This sets up the residue sum that yields the functional equation on the next (missing) page of the paper.
errors: The text says ζ vanishes 'lorsque s est égal à un nombre entier négatif'; Riemann's original says 'negative gerade Zahl' (negative even integer). As written this is false: ζ(-1)=-1/12, ζ(-3)=1/120. The word 'pair' is omitted in this French copy.

The last sentence reads 'pour des valeurs de s à module infiniment grand'. Mathematically, and in Riemann's German ('durch die Werthe von unendlich großem Modul'), this refers to values of the integration variable x of infinitely large modulus, not s. This is a copying/translation slip.

Unjustified as written (as in the original, which is equally terse): the vanishing of the small circle needs Re s>1 before continuation. The decay of the large arcs for Re s<0 requires the arcs to avoid the poles 2πin, e.g. radii (2n+1)π.

results.what: Loop (Hankel-type) contour integral representation 2 sin(πs)Γ(s)ζ(s)=i∫_∞^∞(-x)^{s-1}/(e^x-1)dx giving the analytic continuation of ζ to C\{1}
results.modern_name: Riemann's contour-integral continuation of the zeta function (Hankel contour)

results.what: Trivial zeros of ζ at negative (even) integers and meromorphy with a single pole at s=1
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (values at negative integers, 1749 heuristically); Riemann 1859 rigorous

results.what: Deforming the contour to the exterior for Re s<0 to pick up residues at 2πin (start of the functional equation proof)
results.modern_name: First proof of the functional equation of ζ

deep.surprise_reason: This is a French translation/copy of the first page of Riemann's published 1859 prime-number paper; the content is exactly his well-known published argument. The only deviations are copying slips (omitted 'pair', s for x).

checkable.asserts: e^{-iπs}-e^{iπs} = -2i sin(πs), so multiplying the loop integral by i gives 2 sin(πs)Γ(s)ζ(s)
equals -1/12, nonzero: ζ does not vanish at all negative integers (the page's statement needs 'even')
all equal 0: trivial zeros at negative even integers
ζ(-m)=(-1)^m B_{m+1}/(m+1) at m=3 (residue computation); result 0
equals 1: the integrand at s=1 has residue 1, giving the pole of ζ at s=1
reflection formula: the prefactor equals Γ(1-s)/π, whose only poles are at s=1,2,3,...

transcription_corrections: 'analytique$_x$' — the subscript-like mark after 'analytique' is likely a comma or stray mark, not a subscript x.
Second-to-last sentence: the manuscript indeed reads 'un nombre entier négatif' (no 'pair'); the transcription is faithful, but the manuscript text is mathematically deficient.
Final sentence: the manuscript reads 'valeurs de s'; the transcription is faithful, though mathematically 'x' is meant.
Integral limits '∫_∞^∞': the manuscript shows ∞ as both limits, consistent with the loop from +∞ to +∞.
